meta.move: Strong path: owns the missed call, then evidence in order, then the rewrite
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty minutes, Hale. Owen found out about a zero on his phone in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
Ms. Kalinowski, thank you for coming in. Before anything else: I entered that zero before I called you, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.
Okay. Now tell me what you based it on.

Here's what I can show you. The document's version history: created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due, title only. At 11:52, 612 words arrive in one edit. At 11:58, another 794. No drafts before that.

Turn the screen, I want to read it myself. 11:31, 11:52, 612 words, 11:58, 794 words; I'm writing that down. Owen wrote it over the weekend, so a paste into a fresh file proves where he typed it, not who wrote it.
Second, the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the scene; you can search it yourself.
Give me the text, Hale. A misquote is a careless student, not a machine. Whatever happens next, this stays off his record and it stays quiet.

Our procedure allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. We could do it in my room, Thursday at 8:15, with the vice-principal supervising.

Before class, just the vice-principal, nobody else in the room or told about it? Then to put this behind him, Thursday at 8:15, and I want "nothing goes on file" in an email from you tonight. And until then, that zero comes out of the gradebook he can see on his phone.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In today's meeting you proposed a supervised rewrite in your room on Thursday at 8:15, with the vice-principal supervising, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing going on Owen's record. I still require that it stay private, that the zero come out of the gradebook he can see until then, and that you confirm "nothing goes on file" in writing. I expect that email from you tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: last position, agreeing to the Thursday 8:15 supervised rewrite on condition it stays private, the zero comes out of the gradebook now, and "nothing goes on file" arrives in writing.
What moved her: "At 11:52, 612 words arrive in one edit," because it was exact, timestamped, tied to Owen's own file and something she could check herself.
What cost ground: nothing.
Try next time: before ending, answer her three conditions out loud, especially taking the zero out of the gradebook, so the deal is closed in the room rather than left for her email.
